text:
Tara: Escalation from ACME — their chat responses intermittently stop mid-sentence. Happens over SSE and websocket fallback. Customer reports long gaps where no tokens arrive, then sometimes final chunk never comes. Asking for repro artifacts so we can triage.

Alice: Thanks — two quick asks up front: one or more request_id values + approximate timestamps, and a minimal repro (curl/wscat) from their network path. Also need model, SDK version, and whether they use our hosted API or a private proxy.

Tara: Provided one request id: req_01GPX3K2MB8Y7 — observed cutoff at 2026-03-15 18:12:03 UTC. Client: browser via JS SDK v0.9.2 behind Cloudflare. They said it happens ~3-4x/day for a subset of users.

Devon: Good. Please ask them to paste the raw response headers they receive (content-type, transfer-encoding, x-redwood-request-id, x-edge-id). Also have them run this curl SSE repro from the same network path and paste the raw terminal output (don't format):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"Say a long sentence with pauses","stream":true}' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat'
```

Sanjay: For websocket repro, wscat is helpful. Example: 

```
wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# then send: {"type":"input","text":"<long input>"}
```

Devon: Also ask for a browser HAR (DevTools -> Network -> Save HAR with content). If they have a corporate proxy/NAT, pcap or ngrep from their edge is golden: 

```
sudo tcpdump -w capture.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443
# or (ngrep requires listening before TLS termination):
sudo ngrep -W byline -d any 'POST /v1/chat' tcp and port 443
```

Alice: We'll need to correlate req_01GPX3K2MB8Y7 across our edge logs and runtime. Tara — when you have the HAR/pcap/curl output, upload to the support upload link and paste the upload id + the exact timestamp window (+/- 60s) here so we can pull logs.

support-bot: Reminder — to create an internal debug bundle for the runtime team, use the support endpoint (customer-facing):

```
# internal debug bundle tool (support)
curl -X POST "https://support.redwood.ai/debug-bundle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <support-token>" \
  -F "request_id=req_01GPX3K2MB8Y7" \
  -F "start_time=2026-03-15T18:11:30Z" \
  -F "end_time=2026-03-15T18:12:30Z"
```

Devon: From infra side, check for these signatures when correlating:
- connection resets (RST) or upstream 502/504 around the timestamp
- SSE frames stop but socket remains open (suggests client/proxy buffering)
- double CRLF or malformed chunk boundaries (proxy buffer flush issues)
- differences between edge and runtime bytes_sent counters

If SSE frames stop but the TCP connection is still established, try to rule out client buffering by running the curl repro from the same network. If curl shows the tokens streaming correctly but browser doesn't, suspect intermediary (Cloudflare, corporate proxy) or browser buffering. If curl also stops, check pcap for FIN/RST or TLS session termination.

Sanjay: One more ask: include the exact SDK call and params (max_tokens, stop sequences, temperature), and whether they set any client-side request timeouts. Also confirm they didn't hit a 429 right before the broken stream — rate-limiter responses sometimes leave the socket in a weird state.

Tara: I'll collect the artifacts (HAR, pcap, curl output) and upload now. Will paste the upload id + window here when available. If we can't reproduce within 24h after collecting, I'll escalate to runtime on-call and include the debug bundle. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
